NFL.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, it has lost so far.
NFL.evidence: 0 of 3 graded games (NYG over NO, ATL over CHI, PHI over CAR) where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite.
NFL.test: On past seasons, take every game where the model's pick differs from the moneyline favorite. Compare its win rate and spread record with Vegas. Wait for 20+ games.

NFL.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
NFL.evidence: 0 of 3 graded games with a gap of 4.9 points or more (CHI 6.6, CAR 5.2, BAL 4.9) won the over/under pick. Overall over/under is 4-8.
NFL.test: On past seasons, group games by size of the total gap (under 2, 2-4, over 4). Check hit rate per group. Needs 20+ games in the large-gap group.

NFL.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
NFL.evidence: In 5 of the 7 games where the winner was wrong, the review names efficiency as a main reason.
NFL.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

NFL.lesson: Big-game player picks hit less often than the model's chances say.
NFL.evidence: 1 of 8 big-game picks hit, against 2.8 expected. The milestone picks went 6 of 8, against 6.0 expected.
NFL.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for 300+ yard and similar long-shot props, in buckets of model chance. Needs 20+ picks.

NFL.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are underperforming.
NFL.evidence: 1 of 5 best-value picks hit this season, against 2.7 expected, at -3.09 units.
NFL.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks.

College.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern may not hold up.
College.evidence: By my count in the Week 7-8 results listed, the over hit in 8 of 13 games where the model total was 3+ above Vegas (Week 7: 6 of 10; Week 8: 2 of 3). That is only slightly better than a coin flip, and the sample is under 20.
College.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Need 20+ games per group.

College.lesson: Big misses mostly show up as efficiency gaps; turnovers and finishing drives come second.
College.evidence: In the 24 games missed by 8+ points in the earlier set, the top listed reason was efficiency in 17, turnovers in 4, finishing drives in 2 and defensive touchdowns in 1. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss. Week 8 results had no reviews, so no new data.
College.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin and points per trip inside the 40 with the long-run average, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

College.lesson: When the model picks a different favorite than Vegas, early results are mixed, not bad.
College.evidence: Now 6 games with a different favorite: the model was right in 3 (Missouri State, Army, Marshall) and wrong in 3 (Cincinnati, Old Dominion, Rice over Tulsa). The earlier 1-for-4 has evened out. Sample is tiny.
College.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

College.lesson: When the model has the favorite winning by 3+ more points than Vegas, the favorite has mostly not covered.
College.evidence: In the Week 7-8 results listed, by my count 9 games fit (Utah, Fresno State, Houston, UCLA, NC State, Air Force, UConn, James Madison, Florida International). The favorite covered in 2 (UCLA over Wisconsin, UConn) and failed in 7. The earlier 6-for-6 count included games not in this list, and UCLA over Wisconsin contradicts a perfect record. Today's BYU (gap 8.4) and Troy (6.8) and Ohio (9.0) fit.
College.test: On past seasons, take games where the model's favorite margin is 3+ points above Vegas's and check the cover rate by size of gap (3-6, 6+). Need 20+ games per group.

College.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak so far.
College.evidence: This season the list is 2 of 7 against 3.6 expected, at -3.18 units. Seven games is far too few to read, and the edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed).
College.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Need 20+ games per bucket.
